text:
nora: quick dump from today's allocator surgery run. trying a soft-reserve + preemptible-coalesce flow to reduce blocking during nvme spill storms.

nora: gist: when fallback coalesce would block we enqueue range with state=soft_reserved, worker tries async merge. alloc can steal soft_reserved ranges under pressure.

ef rain: can you paste the state bits you used? curious about race surface.

nora: sure, header is a single 32-bit word: 
```
bit0: allocated
bit1: free
bit2: reserved
bit3: merging
bit4: soft_reserved
bits5-15: owner_cpu
bits16-31: checksum
```

nora: soft_reserved means "prefer worker" but allow alloc borrow if memory_pressure>threshold. borrow is an atomic CAS from soft_reserved->allocated. worker aborts if CAS fails.

tomas: Interesting. How do you measure memory_pressure? global watermark or tenant-local?

nora: tenant-local pressure: (resident_pages / tenant_commit_limit) and a burst factor from recent spill_rate. threshold 0.85 by default.

ef rain: two quick concerns: 1) if many allocs steal ranges, worker will spin requeueing the same ranges repeatedly; 2) how to avoid double-free if worker was mid-merge?

nora: for 1) worker uses exponential backoff per-range and increases merge_cost_budget. after N fails it demotes to background scan instead of busy retry.

nora: for 2) merge is write-once: worker constructs merged header off-CPU and does a single atomic swap of header pointer; if CAS fails, it abandons; free path must check a merge_in_progress bit and respect owner_cpu stamp.

tomas: sounds safer. what about telemetry? we need visibility into preemptions and requeues.

nora: added metrics: soft_reserve_count, soft_reserve_steal_count, worker_requeue_count, merge_abort_cas_failures, avg_merge_latency_ms. sample from canary: 
```
soft_reserve_count=412
soft_reserve_steal_count=73
worker_requeue_count=28
merge_abort_cas_failures=6
avg_merge_latency_ms=2.1
```

watcher-bot: canary-deploy 2026.03.29-alloc-psi succeeded at 1843220021 :white_check_mark:

efrain: those steal numbers look acceptable. did you also compare nvme spill delta?

nora: yes: spill_ops_before=12/min, after=9/min for mixed workload; but one tenant with very bursty small frees saw spill_ops increase slightly.

tomas: maybe steal_policy should be tenant-aware — disable stealing for tenants marked "no-steal" (e.g., private infra) and only allow soft_preempt for shared hosts.

nora: agreed. also added an emergency-flush hook: if spill_rate rises >20% in 2m, worker moves to high-priority and aggressively merges small fragments.

efrain: what about interactions with the paging path? if a page fault happens while merge in progress, could we block user threads?

nora: we avoided blocking by keeping merge atomic and non-blocking: user PF handler will see merged header or original; no stall. if PF requires reading metadata we ensure it's lockless read.

tomas: long-term thought: fold coalesce hints into the eviction scoring so spiller picks victims that enable better future merges. e.g., prefer victims that create coalescible neighbors.

efrain: that is neat but couples spiller and allocator heuristics. worth an RFC.

watcher-bot: perf-run tid=9002 microbatch-mix finished at 1843220048 :bar_chart:

nora: next steps: 1) add per-tenant steal_enable flag (default true for Hosted? false for Private) 2) tune backoff and merge_budget, 3) add dashboard: steal_rate, requeue_rate, spill_delta.

tomas: also add an automated safety switch: if worker_requeue_count > 200 in 10m, auto-disable soft_reserve for that tenant and open an alert.

efrain: +1. and CI: add chaos test where worker thread killed mid-merge to validate TTL/cleanup.

deploy-bot: pushed patchset alloc/soft-reserve v1.2 to canary at 1843220056 :rocket:

nora: thanks all. i'll drop the short RFC link in here and include microbench numbers. attach repro script and flamegraphs when ready.
